evals.prompt: We support monthly immunization camps in 48 villages in Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Each camp runs on a fixed day each month, 9am to 2pm, at the anganwadi center. Our register knows every enrolled child's next due dose and the camp date. Barrier work (exit interviews at 12 camps plus a household survey of 600 mothers) found that mothers of children who missed a dose mostly said they forgot which day the camp was or that it was that week; vaccine stock has been reliable for two years and nobody mentioned fees or distrust. The lever brief picked prompts and cues. Audience brief: about 60% of households have a phone, usually held by the husband; many mothers cannot read Hindi SMS; the ASHA visits each hamlet weekly; voice calls in Mewari are feasible through our call center. Design the reminder schedule.
evals.expected_output: A full reminder schedule following the output template: the target behavior and the forgetting barrier carried over with the exit-interview and survey evidence and the note that stock, fees, and distrust were ruled out; the due-date structure as recurring monthly with a fixed camp day known from the register; a schedule table with at least two rows (for example a voice call two days before the camp and a morning-of call or ASHA visit), each with a channel, what it names (the child's name, the dose, the camp day, the anganwadi), and a stop condition (dose recorded, opt-out, ceiling); a frequency ceiling without claiming weekly beats daily as a finding; content requirements that name the action, date, and place and drop loss/gain framing; a channel choice that picks voice in Mewari and the ASHA over Hindi SMS because of literacy and phones held by husbands; a reminders-alone-or-bundled section that applies the Haryana test, notes SMS alone had no impact there, and recommends pairing with the ASHA as messenger (pointing to select-messenger) while leaving incentives as a question for design-incentive-scheme; a decay check with intervals and a trigger; an expected effect that quotes the corrected Thakkar odds ratio, the Kenya 13 to 16 points, the Haryana null, and gives a modest planning range. It does not write the Mewari script, does not re-ask the answered questions, and does not quote a 53% Kenya figure.

evals.prompt: Patients keep missing their follow-up appointments. Set up SMS reminders.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not produce a schedule. It asks the Required questions: the target behavior and the evidence that forgetting, rather than cost, distance, stock, or distrust, is why appointments are missed; how appointments are dated and how the program knows each patient's date; and who holds the phone, whether it is shared, literacy, language, and network. It may ask whether a messenger or incentive is already in the program and whether any reminder data exists, marked optional.

evals.prompt: Patients at our ART clinic in Kisumu, Kenya miss doses. We want to send a daily SMS at 8pm saying 'Take your two tablets now'. The clinic has had three ARV stock-outs this year and some patients share a phone with family. Design the schedule.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces what it safely can: a schedule built on the Kenyan weekly-SMS evidence rather than the requested daily cadence, with a ceiling, an opt-out, and a stop rule, and content requirements that name the patient's own goal or clinic visit rather than a dose instruction. It then states three escalations: because the message concerns medication dosing, a clinician or pharmacist must sign off the content before any send; because the clinic has had stock-outs, reminders cannot work in those months and the supply problem must be raised with the clinic lead first; and because some patients share phones, a privacy review is needed before any message that could disclose HIV status. It names what to bring them. It does not claim weekly beats daily as a finding and does not quote a 53% figure for the Kenyan trial.

evals.prompt: At the camp we want each mother to tell the ASHA when and where she will bring the child for the next dose, and write it on the immunization card. Can you design that?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not run. It says the request is for a plan the mother makes once about a specific upcoming action, not a message the program sends on a schedule, and that this is draft-implementation-intention-prompt's job. It may note that a reminder schedule could later be built around the date the mother wrote down, but it does not produce a schedule here.
